## Purpose

This report explores the structure, completeness, validity, and distributions of the final armed conflict dataset.

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| echo: false

library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)

armed_conflict_data <- read_csv(
  "../Data/Processed/armed_conflict_final_data.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE,
  na = c("", "NA")
)

binary_variables <- c("armed_conflict", "earthquake", "drought", "oecd")
continuous_variables <- c(
  "infant_mortality", "maternal_mortality", "neonatal_mortality",
  "under5_mortality", "gdp_1000", "pop_dens", "urban", "age_dep",
  "male_edu", "temp", "rainfall_1000"
)
```

## Structure of the data

The dataset contains `r nrow(armed_conflict_data)` observations and `r ncol(armed_conflict_data)` variables, representing `r n_distinct(armed_conflict_data$iso)` countries over the years `r min(armed_conflict_data$year)`--`r max(armed_conflict_data$year)`.

```{r}
#| label: variable-structure

structure_table <- tibble(
  variable = names(armed_conflict_data),
  data_type = map_chr(armed_conflict_data, ~ paste(class(.x), collapse = ", "))
)

kable(structure_table, caption = "Variables, data types")
```

The first and last six observations help confirm the ordering and content of the data.

```{r}
#| label: head-tail

head(armed_conflict_data)
tail(armed_conflict_data)
```


## Missing data

```{r}
#| label: missingness

missing_summary <- armed_conflict_data |>
  summarise(across(everything(), ~ sum(is.na(.x)))) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "variable", values_to = "n_missing") |>
  mutate(percent_missing = 100 * n_missing / nrow(armed_conflict_data)) |>
  arrange(desc(n_missing))

kable(
  missing_summary,
  digits = 1,
  caption = "Missing values by variable"
)
```


Missing observations are retained as `NA`. A complete-case dataset will be created later for a specific model, using the variables required by that model. There is high missingness in maternal mortality which will be further considered when interpreting results.

## Summary statistics

Year and binary indicators are excluded from continuous summaries because their means and standard deviations do not describe continuous distributions meaningfully.

```{r}
#| label: numerical-summary

numerical_summary <- armed_conflict_data |>
  summarise(across(
    all_of(continuous_variables),
    list(
      n = ~ sum(!is.na(.x)),
      mean = ~ mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
      median = ~ median(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
      sd = ~ sd(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
      min = ~ min(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
      max = ~ max(.x, na.rm = TRUE)
    )
  )) |>
  pivot_longer(
    everything(),
    names_to = c("variable", ".value"),
    names_pattern = "(.*)_(n|mean|median|sd|min|max)$"
  ) |>
  select(variable, n, mean, median, sd, min, max)

kable(numerical_summary, digits = 2, caption = "Summary statistics for continuous variables")
```

Although stored numerically, the four indicator variables are categorical. Their frequency tables include both counts and percentages.

```{r}
#| label: categorical-summary

categorical_summary <- armed_conflict_data |>
  select(all_of(binary_variables)) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "variable", values_to = "value") |>
  count(variable, value, name = "frequency") |>
  group_by(variable) |>
  mutate(percent = 100 * frequency / sum(frequency)) |>
  ungroup()

kable(categorical_summary, digits = 1, caption = "Frequency tables for categorical variables")
```

## Distributions and potential outliers

```{r}
#| label: histograms
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 12
#| fig-cap: "Histograms of continuous variables; scales differ across panels"

armed_conflict_data |>
  select(all_of(continuous_variables)) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "variable", values_to = "value") |>
  ggplot(aes(value)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "#3B82A0", colour = "white", na.rm = TRUE) +
  facet_wrap(vars(variable), scales = "free", ncol = 3) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Count") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
#| label: boxplots
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 12
#| fig-cap: "Boxplots of continuous variables; points beyond the whiskers are candidates for investigation"

armed_conflict_data |>
  select(all_of(continuous_variables)) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "variable", values_to = "value") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = "", y = value)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "#A7C7D3", outlier.alpha = 0.35, na.rm = TRUE) +
  facet_wrap(vars(variable), scales = "free", ncol = 3) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(), axis.ticks.x = element_blank())
```
